verdicts.title: AdaClip accounting accepts invalid parameters on direct construction; num_groups=0 silently prices adaptive clipping as free
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. _adaclip.py:23-37 is a frozen slots dataclass with no __post_init__; validation exists only in the adaclip() factory (:139-156). Siblings Poisson (_poisson.py:37-61), ParallelPoisson (_parallel_poisson.py:23-36), RandomAllocation (_random_allocation.py:67-77) and KOutOfT (_k_out_of_t.py:40-47) all validate in __post_init__, and _poisson.py carries an explicit comment saying the reason is that direct construction and deserialization bypass the factory. Executed: AdaClip(inner=Gaussian(1.1), fraction_noise_std=0.05, expected_batch_size=250.0, num_groups=0).effective_noise_multiplier == 1.1 (bare Gaussian) and poisson(...).pld().epsilon_at(1e-5) == 0.14229070057507137 vs 0.14276055192086845 at num_groups=1 and 0.1441761381215057 at num_groups=4. Also reproduced through the real serialization path: state_dict of a valid num_groups=4 process, edited to num_groups=0, reloads via from_state_dict with no error and reports 0.14229 instead of 0.14418 (~1.3% under). Negative fraction_noise_std=-0.05 and expected_batch_size=-250.0 are accepted and produce the same z_eff as their positive counterparts (sign lost in the sigma_b square). Corrections to the report: negative num_groups does NOT pass silently (-1 and -4 raise OverflowError from the PyO3 unsigned conversion), so only 0 is the fail-open value. Severity lowered from medium to low: every in-repo construction site (_dp_trainer.py:4245, examples/train_sft.py:1821, train_dpo.py:2312, train_dpsgd.py:1568) goes through the validated adaclip() factory, so the under-report requires a caller to supply a nonsensical value or to hand-edit/corrupt a checkpoint, and the magnitude is ~1%. Still genuine and cheap to fix, and it is an anti-conservative (under-charging) silence rather than a fail-closed error. Not a duplicate of open #345 ('Bind AdaClip released statistic to the parameters the accountant charges'): that issue is about the runtime-to-accountant binding of the released quantile statistic, whereas this is a missing constructor-level validator of the #336/#516 normalization family (both closed).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: AdaClip is a public exported type (opaque.dpsgd.accounting.types.AdaClip) and the generic DpProcess codec rebuilds it with cls(**kwargs) on load, so both direct construction and deserialization skip the adaclip() factory's checks. Constructing or restoring AdaClip with num_groups=0 makes _native.adaclip_sensitivity return 1/nm, so effective_noise_multiplier equals the bare Gaussian's and the noisy clipping-fraction release is charged as free: epsilon_at(1e-5) drops from 0.14418 (num_groups=4) to 0.14229 with no warning. fraction_noise_std<0 and expected_batch_size<0 are likewise accepted, silently aliased to their absolute values by the sigma_b square. Negative num_groups does raise (OverflowError from the native u-int conversion), so 0 is the only silently-accepted invalid value.

verdicts.title: Sampler RNG streams are exempt from the #728 namespaced-root convention and can collide byte-identically
verdicts.reasoning: The mechanical facts check out. PoissonSampler seeds numpy from the caller's key verbatim (_poisson.py:108 'self.generator = np.random.default_rng(key.seed)'), KOutOfTSampler likewise (_k_out_of_t.py:58), and RandomAllocationSampler derives each epoch from a bare integer fold (_random_allocation.py:125 'np.random.default_rng(fold_in(self._key, epoch).seed)'). No sampler declares a string stream root; packages/opaque-engine/tests/rng/test_stream_root_namespacing.py enumerates every internal root (paired, dpsgd.gaussian, dpsgd.adaptive_clipping, dpftrl.mf_gaussian, dpftrl.second_moment.*, auditing.*) and no sampler appears, and the tag table at docs/reference/rng.md:215-222 lists no sampler tag. The stated normative convention at rng.md:208-212 ('A mechanism that draws randomness folds one unique string tag into the key it was given') does cover samplers on its face, so the gap is real. Verified numerically that fold_in(K, 3).seed equals the seed RandomAllocationSampler derives internally for epoch 3, and that split(K, 3) == [fold_in(K, i)], so the key material genuinely aliases. Severity kept at low and I deflate the consequence further than the reporter did: the collision surface is sampler-to-sampler only. Namespaced noise mechanisms consume their keys through torch generator_from_key while samplers use numpy PCG64, so even an aliased seed yields uncorrelated numbers across those two families; and a training run uses one sampler, so no shipped or documented configuration hands one base key to two samplers. Also correcting the report's wording: PoissonSampler draws rng.random(n) while RandomAllocationSampler draws rng.integers(0, num_bins, n), so the two are driven by an identical bit stream but the inclusion decisions are coupled, not 'identical'. No open issue covers sampler RNG namespacing (#320 and #356 are about sampler-to-accountant binding, not domain separation), so already_tracked stays 0.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Samplers are the one family of randomness-drawing components that never fold a namespaced string root into the key they are handed, contrary to the convention published at docs/reference/rng.md:208-212 and enforced for every noise/auditing stream by packages/opaque-engine/tests/rng/test_stream_root_namespacing.py. Verified aliasing: RandomAllocationSampler(key=K) derives epoch e from fold_in(K, e), which is byte-identical to the key material a user creates with the documented per-rank idiom fold_in(K, rank) for rank==e and to split(K, n)[e]. A caller who hands one base key to two samplers (or hands a sampler a key it also derives sibling keys from) gets deterministically coupled subsampling with nothing to signal it. No current example or documented flow does this, and namespaced noise mechanisms are insulated because they draw through torch generators rather than numpy PCG64, so no shipped epsilon is affected; the item is a hardening/consistency gap, not a live defect.

verdicts.title: clipping.md accounting snippets call dpsgd_acc without ever importing it
verdicts.reasoning: Verified by reading the file. docs/user-guide/clipping.md:236 does 'import opaque.accounting as acc' and then :239-241 call dpsgd_acc.poisson / dpsgd_acc.adaclip / dpsgd_acc.gaussian; :559 repeats the same unused import and :566 calls dpsgd_acc.poisson / dpsgd_acc.gaussian. grep over the whole file shows the only 'import opaque...' lines are :236, :259 (opaque.distributed) and :559 — 'as dpsgd_acc' never appears, and 'acc' is never used. Every other docs page that uses the alias defines it ('import opaque.dpsgd.accounting as dpsgd_acc' in quickstart.md:16, accounting.md:48, dp-sgd.md:30, index.md:78, precision.md:69, gaussian.md:127, mechanisms/index.md:114 and all six tutorials), so clipping.md is the outlier. The reporter's secondary point also holds: acc.poisson does not exist on the cross-cutting facade (opaque.accounting re-exports composition/calibration; the DP-SGD factories live on opaque.dpsgd.accounting), so the obvious substitution fails too. Kept at low and I deflate the framing slightly: both fenced blocks are illustrative pseudo-code that also reference undefined sample_rate / dataset_size / noise_multiplier, so a literal paste would fail regardless; the substantive defect is the wrong (unused) import line contradicting the alias the page then uses. Closed issue #416 ('Execute documentation examples and validate public factory signatures') is the relevant remediation and it is closed, so this is a residual, not a duplicate; open #324 is a broad umbrella about mechanically verifiable claims rather than this concrete slip.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Both accounting blocks on docs/user-guide/clipping.md (AdaClip pricing at :236-247, AUTO-S pricing at :559-568) open with 'import opaque.accounting as acc', never use acc, and then call dpsgd_acc.*, an alias the page never defines — unlike the sixteen other docs pages and six tutorials that all import it as 'import opaque.dpsgd.accounting as dpsgd_acc'. A reader who fixes up the surrounding placeholders and runs the block hits NameError on dpsgd_acc, and the natural repair (using the imported acc) fails again because opaque.accounting exposes no poisson/gaussian/adaclip. Docs-only; no runtime or epsilon impact.

verdicts.title: rng.md example calls gaussian_noise positionally though the factory is keyword-only
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced directly. docs/reference/rng.md:309 reads 'noise_fn, state = gaussian_noise(1.1, key=noise_key)'. The factory at packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/noise/_gaussian.py:156-165 is 'def gaussian_noise(*, noise_multiplier: float, key: RngKey, bound=None, compute_dtype=torch.float32)' — fully keyword-only. Executing the documented call raises TypeError; the exact message is 'gaussian_noise() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 positional argument (and 1 keyword-only argument) were given' (slightly different from the reporter's quoted text, same defect). Note the same page's sibling docs use the correct keyword form, and docs/user-guide/clipping.md:562 writes it correctly as gaussian_noise(noise_multiplier=..., key=...), so :309 is an isolated stale line. Low severity: docs-only, fails loudly and immediately, no epsilon or runtime consequence. Residual of closed #416, not a duplicate of any open issue.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: The canonical training-loop example in the RNG reference (docs/reference/rng.md:309) calls the keyword-only factory positionally. A reader who copies it gets 'TypeError: gaussian_noise() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 positional argument (and 1 keyword-only argument) were given' on the first step. The fix is one word: gaussian_noise(noise_multiplier=1.1, key=noise_key). Docs-only, fails loudly.

verdicts.title: Accounting now rejects sample_rate=1.0 that the runtime PoissonSampler still supports and tests
verdicts.reasoning: Every factual link reproduces. Accounting: _poisson.py:38-41 'if not 0 < sample_rate < 1: raise ValueError'; executed dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(1.1), 1.0) -> 'ValueError: sample_rate must be in (0, 1), got 1.0'. Runtime: packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_poisson.py:89-90 validates '0 < sample_rate <= 1' and executing PoissonSampler(range(10), sample_rate=1.0, n_steps=2, key=key(0)) yields two full batches. The asymmetry is also documented on both sides: docs/user-guide/sampling.md:70 states 'sample_rate float in (0, 1]' for the sampler while the poisson() docstring says 'strictly between zero and one'. Since __post_init__ runs on deserialization, a Poisson process serialized with sample_rate=1.0 no longer loads. However the framing as a 'residual' defect is wrong and I deflate it accordingly: git show 45f41836 (fix(dpsgd): normalize Poisson validation, #516) shows the strict bound was a deliberate change shipped with tests that explicitly pin the rejection — test_rejects_invalid_sample_rate parametrizes [0.0, 1.0, -0.01, 1.01] on both the dataclass and the factory. It is fail-closed, and at q=1 the mathematically correct accountant (dpsgd_acc.gaussian(nm) composed over steps) exists and is reachable. What remains is a documentation/UX inconsistency of low value: the sampler docs advertise (0,1] and the accounting error names no alternative. Not marked as a duplicate of open #356/#320: those track silent runtime-vs-accountant mismatch (fail-open), whereas this is a deliberate over-restriction in the fail-closed direction.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: PoissonSampler accepts and is tested at sample_rate=1.0 (test_sample_rate_one_yields_every_record), and docs/user-guide/sampling.md:70 documents the sampler range as (0, 1], but the accounting dataclass deliberately rejects 1.0 (added in 45f41836 / #516 with tests pinning it), so dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(nm), 1.0) raises 'ValueError: sample_rate must be in (0, 1), got 1.0' and a Poisson process serialized before that change with sample_rate=1.0 no longer deserializes. Mathematically harmless and fail-closed — the correct full-batch accountant is dpsgd_acc.gaussian(nm) composed over steps — so the real defect is documentation: the sampler range in sampling.md contradicts the accounting bound and neither the error nor the docs point to the gaussian() route.

verdicts.title: lambda-CGD noise stream is not RNG-namespaced — sibling gap of the #728 stream-root fix
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced the aliasing exactly. LambdaCgdStrategy.raw_noise_factory (_lambda_cgd.py:152-169) forwards the caller's key unchanged to _make_lambda_cgd_noise, which stores it as MFNoiseState._rng_key and derives per-step torch generators with bare integer folds at :280 ('rng_fold_in(st._rng_key, step)') and :292 ('rng_fold_in(st._rng_key, step - 1)') — no string root anywhere in the file. Contrast the generic MF path, _engine.py:37 MF_GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD='opaque.dpftrl.mf_gaussian' folded in at :167-169 and :395-396, and _mf_gaussian_noise.py:230-239, which routes LambdaCgdStrategy around that engine via the raw_noise_factory hook. Executed repro: mf_gaussian_noise(template, lambda_cgd_strategy(lambda_=0.0, normalized=False), n_steps=5, noise_multiplier=1.0, key=key(42)) produces step-0 and step-1 noise tensors byte-identical to torch.randn(generator=generator_from_key(fold_in(key(42), t))), and split(key(42), 2)[0].seed == fold_in(key(42), 0).seed — i.e. the released noise is exactly what a caller gets from an ordinary integer derivation of the same base key. This is precisely the failure packages/opaque-engine/tests/rng/test_stream_root_namespacing.py describes and guards, and that test cannot catch this mechanism because it enumerates declared root constants and lambda-CGD declares none. Two scope corrections in the repo's favour: (a) the second-moment path is safe — _second_moment.py:92,101 fold SECOND_MOMENT_FIRST/SECOND_STREAM_FOLD before calling _make_raw_mf_noise, so lambda-CGD under second_moment_strategy is namespaced; (b) no in-repo component collides with it today, so the exposure is caller key reuse, not an internal double-draw. The docs claim is fair: rng.md:208-212 states normatively that a mechanism folds one unique string tag into the key it was given, and the tag table at :220 attributes 'opaque.dpftrl.mf_gaussian' to mf_gaussian_noise, which is untrue on the LambdaCgdStrategy dispatch. affects_epsilon kept true but conditional: independence of the released Gaussians is an assumption of the lambda-CGD analysis, and a colliding sibling draw voids it; nothing in the accountant or any test would report it. Severity medium — same class the team judged worth a breaking change in #728, no open issue tracks it (the RNG namespacing issues #374/#728 are both closed).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: mf_gaussian_noise dispatches LambdaCgdStrategy to _make_lambda_cgd_noise via raw_noise_factory, handing it the caller's key unrooted; the mechanism then derives every per-step torch generator as fold_in(key, step). Verified: with key(42) the step-t released noise is torch-equal to torch.randn(generator=generator_from_key(fold_in(key(42), t))) = generator_from_key(split(key(42))[t]) — the caller's own integer key space. Any second component that draws torch noise from a sibling key derived from that same base (split(base), fold_in(base, rank), fold_in(base, step)) therefore draws the identical vector the lambda-CGD mechanism is releasing, breaking the independent-Gaussian assumption the mechanism's sensitivity and accounting rest on, with no error, warning, or accountant signal. Every other Opaque noise stream was namespaced by #728 (MF_GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD, GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD, ADAPTIVE_CLIPPING_STREAM_FOLD, the paired and second-moment roots) and docs/reference/rng.md:208-222 publishes that as a guarantee, which is false for this dispatch path. The second-moment path is unaffected (its key is pre-folded with opaque.dpftrl.second_moment.first), and nothing inside Opaque collides with it today, so the risk is caller key reuse rather than an internal double-draw.
